title: Carrots, canned, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Canned carrots are cooked carrot pieces packed in glass or metal jars without added fat. The product retains most of the nutrients of fresh carrots and is convenient for long‑term storage.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned carrots are often used as an ingredient in soups, stews, and salads.
During canning carrots are usually blanched, which helps preserve their bright orange color.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
A sealed jar can keep canned carrots good for 2‑3 years.
In the US and Canada canned carrots are classified as a ready‑to‑eat vegetable.

items.title: Rich source of vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene in carrots is converted to vitamin A, supporting vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids and vitamin C protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in carrots promotes regular bowel movements and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes this product suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt for preservation; people monitoring sodium intake should take this into account.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to carrots.

items.title: Bacterial contamination if packaging is compromised
items.content: Damaged or bulging cans can harbor pathogenic bacteria; such products should be discarded.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned carrots can be eaten cold in salads, added to hot soups and stews, used in pie fillings, or served as a side dish with meat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer carrots to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 5‑7 days.
